TS2322.explanation: A value of one type was put where a different type is required. TypeScript checks this before the program runs, so it never gets the chance to go wrong.
TS2322.cause: Assigning text to a number variable, or a function returning something other than what it promised.
TS2322.example:
let age: number = "12";               // text into a number
let age: number = Number("12");

TS2345.explanation: An argument passed to a function is not the type that function accepts.
TS2345.cause: Passing a value straight from input, which is always text, into a function expecting a number.

TS2304.explanation: TypeScript reached a name it does not know. Every name must be declared or imported first.
TS2304.cause: A spelling mistake, or a missing import.

TS2339.explanation: The property does not exist on that type. TypeScript knows the shape of the value and this name is not part of it.
TS2339.cause: A spelling mistake, or assuming an object has a field it was never given.

TS2531.explanation: The value might be null, and you used it as if it definitely is not. TypeScript is stopping the crash before it happens.
TS2531.cause: Reading the result of something that can return null without checking it first.

TS18048.explanation: The value might be undefined, and you used it as if it definitely is not.
TS18048.cause: An optional property, or an array lookup that might find nothing.

TS2554.explanation: A function was called with the wrong number of arguments.
TS2554.cause: Forgetting an argument, or changing a function's parameters without updating the calls.

TS7006.explanation: A parameter has no type and TypeScript could not work one out, so it would silently be `any` - which turns off checking for that value.
TS7006.cause: Writing a function without annotating its parameters.
TS7006.example:
function double(n) { return n * 2; }          // n has no type
function doubleOk(n: number) { return n * 2; }

TS2367.explanation: Two values are being compared that can never be equal, because their types have nothing in common. The comparison is always false.
TS2367.cause: Comparing a number with a string, often after forgetting a conversion.

TS2451.explanation: The same name is declared twice in the same scope.
TS2451.cause: Copying a block of code and forgetting to rename the variable, or a let that repeats an earlier one.

TS2552.explanation: TypeScript does not know that name, but it found one that looks very similar and suggests it.
TS2552.cause: A typo. Read the suggestion in the message - it is usually right.

TS1005.explanation: A particular character was expected here and something else was found. The message names the character it wanted.
TS1005.cause: A missing bracket, comma or semicolon - very often on the line above.

TS1109.explanation: A value was expected at that spot and there is nothing usable there.
TS1109.cause: An unfinished expression, such as an assignment with nothing after the equals sign.
TS1109.example:
const x = ;    // nothing to assign
const x = 0;

TS2740.explanation: An object was given where a type with more required fields was expected, and several of those fields are missing.
TS2740.cause: Building an object literal by hand and forgetting some of the fields the type requires.

ReferenceError.explanation: At run time, the compiled JavaScript reached a name that does not exist. TypeScript catches most of these before running, so this usually comes from code it could not check.
ReferenceError.cause: Using a value typed as `any`, or a name that only exists in some environments.
ReferenceError.example:
// Give values real types instead of any, and TypeScript will catch
// this class of mistake before the program runs at all.

TypeError.explanation: At run time the compiled JavaScript did something to a value that does not support it - usually reading a property of undefined.
TypeError.cause: A value typed as `any`, or data from outside the program that did not have the shape the types claimed.
TypeError.example:
const data = JSON.parse(text) as User;   // 'as' is a promise, not a check
// Check the shape yourself before trusting it.
